In physics, a '''fundamental''' particle<ref>{{#cite:Q1942}}</ref>

* has no substructure
** i.e., is not made of other particles
* has no finite size other than its wavelength $\lambda$

== Types ==

According to the standard model of particle physics, there are three types of fundamental particles: '''[[Lepton|Leptons]], [[Quark|quarks]], and [[Carrier particle|carrier particles]]'''. Each can be roughly divided into three families, of which the first is normal matter, containing stable particles.

[[File:Fundamental particles.jpeg|500px|center]]

Quarks and leptons in family 2 and 3 are observed to decay into stable particles in family 1. The relationship between the different carrier particles is an area of active research.<ref>{{#cite:Q1942}}</ref>
